messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT: spike detected - /v1/generate 5xx rate increased to 18% over 5m. Error sample: \"segfault: model-runner:kv-cache double free\". Triggering page to #incidents and oncall.
alex: seeing same in metrics. Affected region: us-west-2, model-pool 'gptx-quant-8bit' heavily hit. Latency up too. :frowning:
jordan_sre: logs show repeated SIGSEGV from model-runtime PID 4321 on node gpu-07. OOM not obvious, looks like heap corruption. Attaching recent stderr tail:

```
[2026-03-15T14:03:12Z] model-runner[4321]: segfault at 0x7ffdeadbeef ip 0x55a1c4 offset 0x1a
[2026-03-15T14:03:12Z] model-runner[4321]: backtrace: runtime::kv_cache::evict+0x12f
[2026-03-15T14:03:13Z] kernel: Out of bounds write detected in GPU driver
```
maya_eng: that function is in the new continuous-batching change from last week. Could be a use-after-free under high concurrency.
tina_ops: impact scope: ~2.8k requests/min failing, 14 customer apps reported increased 5xx. Support queue ticked up 30%.
ryan_support: flagged high-severity customer "Atlas Analytics" seeing timeouts on realtime embedding pipelines — they're in production. Contacted account rep.
eng-runner: can we immediately shift traffic off the quantized variant? Propose fallback to model-pool 'gptx-fp16' until we patch.
alex: agreed. Steps I can do now:
1) update routing rule for us-west-2 to prefer gptx-fp16 (lower perf but stable)
2) scale up fp16 pool by +4 nodes
3) cordon gpu-07 and drain model-runtime pods for investigation
Is that OK?
jordan_sre: do 1 and 3 now. For draining, use this command:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-07 && kubectl drain gpu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
``` 
I'll watch for evictions.
maya_eng: while draining, add runtime flag to disable continuous-batching on fp16 fallback to reduce concurrency pressure: `--batching=off` if supported.
alex: applying routing change now. Patching canary first.
oncall-bot: DEPLOY BOT: routing-change v2026.03.15-canary started by alex. Links: https://console/redwood/routes/changes/7882
alex: canary successful for 10% traffic. Monitoring errors.
(2m later)
alex: canary looks good, proceeding to 100% for us-west-2. Errors dropping to 2.1%.
jordan_sre: gpu-07 drained successfully. Collected core dump and logs to /var/logs/cores/gpu-07-core-4321.tar.gz. Uploaded to internal S3: s3://redwood-incident-dumps/gpu-07/4321.tar.gz
maya_eng: starting bisect on batching patch. Initial hypothesis: under concurrent KV cache writes we hit a race that double frees a buffer.
tina_ops: customer impact update: 2 customers currently experiencing errors post-fallback, others recovered. Notifying enterprise reps and updating status page.
ryan_support: noted. Sent message to Atlas Analytics: we routed traffic to a stable variant and have engineering working on a root cause. ETA for full restoration TBD. They want a timeline.
li_pm: severity? Recommend Sev2 — customer-facing degraded service across multiple customers but partial mitigation in place.
alex: agreed Sev2. Setting incident doc: https://docs.internal/incidents/2234567890
eng-runner: quick patch idea: add guard in kv_cache::evict to check pointer validity, build hotfix branch, run unit with ASAN and stress harness.
maya_eng: I can cut a hotfix branch now. If tests pass in 30-45m we can roll a restart-based fix.
jordan_sre: caution: rolling restart will cause brief increased latency. Coordinate with traffic shaping.
alex: scheduling rolling restart across pool in 10m after hotfix build. Meanwhile keep routing to fp16.
oncall-bot: NOTE: Next oncall for incidents is eng-oncall: sara. Handoff required at 15:30 UTC. Current assignee: alex.
alex: tagging @sara for handoff. Sara: I'll leave a concise playbook in the incident doc: what we did, where dumps live, how to revert routing.
sara: acknowledged. I'll join in 10m for the restart window.
(40m later)
maya_eng: hotfix branch built and passes stress with ASAN flagged freed-use in a loop but patch validated to prevent double-free. Preparing canary build.
eng-runner: canary rollout of patched runtime to 5 pods in us-west-2.
oncall-bot: DEPLOY BOT: runtime-hotfix-canary v2026.03.15-hotfix started by maya_eng
maya_eng: canary looks stable for 8m. No segfaults in canary pods.
alex: starting gradual rollout + routing back to original quantized pool after we confirm stability. Will keep fallback for Atlas until final confirmation.
tina_ops: status page updated: partial mitigation in place, degraded service for small subset of customers. Next update in 30m or on resolution.
ryan_support: Atlas responded: appreciated the update, will wait for final fix before fully switching their pipeline.
(handoff summary)
alex: HANDOFF -> sara: current state: routing changed to fp16 for us-west-2, fallback in place for Atlas, hotfix rolling out (canary passed), core dump uploaded, logs link in incident doc. Action items for next oncall:
- monitor error rate, keep last_message_ts in thread updated
- complete full rollout of hotfix if no regressions
- coordinate rolling restart if needed for any remaining problematic nodes
- postmortem owners: maya_eng (root cause + patch), jordan_sre (for dumps and triage), alex (mitigation & communication)
sara: acknowledged. I'll take over monitoring and post updates every 15m until resolved.
maya_eng: note for postmortem: include stress harness results and reproduce steps for continuous-batching sequence length >4096.
ryan_support: will prepare customer-facing summary and timeline for Atlas and notify CS once final fix in prod.
alex: setting incident status to 'mitigated' for now (errors down to 0.7%). Will set to resolved when hotfix fully rolled and no recurrences for 2h.
sara: copy that. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
